cvEn:
Yaakov Levanon, son of Yafa and Eliyahu, was born on 6 Adar II 5689 (18 March 1929) in Safed. His childhood was spent in the moshava of Sejera in the Lower Galilee, where he absorbed the spirit of nobility and heroism of the tradition of the HaShomer guards. As a youth he loved to travel around the country, and he also tried his hand at writing poetry.

At a young age he enlisted in the British Army and joined the Jewish Brigade. Even while abroad he was careful to observe Jewish customs, including Sabbath observance and kashrut. During the struggle against British rule he was arrested several times and was held in Latrun. He aspired to study cinema and even received a permit to travel to America for further training. However, when the War of Independence broke out following the UN General Assembly resolution of 29 November 1947 on the partition of Eretz Israel into two states, he gave up his aspiration and immediately reported for service.

Yaakov Shevach took part in the defense of Jerusalem, and when the British withdrew he served in the Etzion Bloc. He was among the last to break into the Old City and defended its Jewish residents. He held out there until 26 May 1948, two days before the surrender of the Old City. On that day he was seriously wounded by a grenade and died the next day, on 18 Iyar 5708 (27 May 1948).

His younger brother, Moshe-Yosef, also fell in the War of Independence. In memory of the two sons, their bereaved father published a memorial book in 5709 (1949) titled "Sihim KeArazim" ("Shrubs Like Cedars"). Yaakov's name is inscribed on the memorial at the military cemetery on Mount Herzl, commemorating the fallen of the Jewish Quarter and the fighters who fell in the battle for Jerusalem and were buried on the Mount of Olives.
